entities.name: Adrianos Komnenos
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adrianos Komnenos was a Byzantine aristocrat and general of the late eleventh and early twelfth centuries, a younger brother of Emperor Alexios I Komnenos. Like other Komnenian siblings, he was woven into the family's system of shared rule: high titles, military commands, and marriage alliances that turned the imperial family into the state's central institution after 1081.

Adrianos appears in the Alexiad and related sources as a trusted kinsman in the wars and court politics that stabilised Byzantium after Manzikert and the Norman invasions. The Komnenian habit of elevating brothers and in-laws created a dynastic aristocracy that replaced much of the older Anatolian military elite.

His career exemplifies how Alexios rebuilt imperial power as a family consortium—effective against external enemies, but binding the empire's fortunes to Komnenian kinship solidarity.
